 Ramayana crosses Rs 1,483 crore globally to become fifth biggest Indian film
 Ranbir Kapoor starrer overtakes Dhurandhar, RRR and KGF Chapter 2, with Pushpa 2 now in its sights
 Published
 14 hours ago on
 November 18, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 MUMBAI: Ramayana’s box office journey is turning into an epic of its own. But while Lord Ram’s cinematic adventure continues to draw audiences, the film’s latest milestone has put some formidable blockbusters in its rear-view mirror. The Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi starrer has taken its worldwide gross to Rs 1,483.10 crore by Day 13, making it the fifth-highest-grossing Indian film of all time, according to Sacnilk estimates.
 The film has now moved ahead of Dhurandhar, RRR and KGF Chapter 2 in the all-time worldwide rankings. Its next target is Pushpa 2: The Rule, although the journey up the chart may require a stronger hold at the domestic box office.
 Despite its impressive global tally, Ramayana recorded some moderation in India on its 13th day. Sacnilk estimates that the film collected Rs 28.35 crore net across 22,551 shows, taking its domestic total to Rs 820.95 crore net and Rs 981.10 crore gross.
 Overseas markets added another Rs 12 crore gross on Day 13, lifting the international total to Rs 502 crore. The domestic and overseas figures together put the worldwide gross at Rs 1,483.10 crore.
 The Hindi version remained the biggest contributor to the film’s India collections, earning Rs 20.75 crore on Day 13 across 17,867 shows.
 The regional-language versions added to the tally, with Malayalam contributing Rs 2.35 crore, Kannada Rs 2 crore, Tamil Rs 1.75 crore and Telugu Rs 1.50 crore.
 Ramayana had opened with Rs 64.85 crore at the Indian box office, followed by Rs 48.05 crore on its first Friday. The film’s subsequent run has taken it past the Rs 800 crore domestic net mark, although the latest daily figures suggest that its pace is beginning to moderate.
 Trade analyst Taran Adarsh had earlier described the film’s second Monday performance as “superb”, pointing to its ability to cross Rs 20 crore on a regular working day as an indication of audience acceptance. He had also noted that sustaining similar collections through the second week would be important for the film’s overall box office performance.
 That question of staying power is now central to its next phase. A large opening and a strong overseas contribution have put Ramayana among India’s biggest theatrical successes, but its daily domestic collections will determine how much further it can climb.
 At Rs 1,483.10 crore worldwide, Ramayana has moved past Dhurandhar, which finished its theatrical run at Rs 1,307.35 crore, RRR at Rs 1,230 crore and KGF Chapter 2 at Rs 1,215 crore, according to Sacnilk.
 The next position is occupied by Pushpa 2: The Rule, with a reported worldwide collection of Rs 1,742.10 crore. That leaves Ramayana around Rs 259 crore short of fourth place.
 The three films ahead of Pushpa 2 are Dangal, with Rs 2,070.30 crore, Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge at Rs 1,813.39 crore and Baahubali 2: The Conclusion at Rs 1,788.06 crore.
 The rankings put Ramayana in some heavyweight company, but the gap between its current collection and the films above it is still substantial. Its next few days will be crucial in determining whether it can move closer to the top four or settle into fifth place.
 Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana has been mounted on a reported budget of Rs 4,000 crore, making it one of the most ambitious and expensive projects in Indian cinema.
 The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram and Sai Pallavi as Sita, alongside Yash, Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey and Lara Dutta. Its scale, star cast and retelling of one of India’s best-known epics have made it a major theatrical event.
 For now, the film has already crossed several major box office milestones in less than a fortnight. Whether it can bridge the roughly Rs 259 crore gap to Pushpa 2 will depend on how well it holds its audience in the days ahead. The epic has cleared another milestone; the next chapter of its box office story is still being written.
